questions.q: In T-SQL, what turns a BACKUP DATABASE statement into a differential backup instead of another full backup?
options: Adding the WITH DIFFERENTIAL clause
Adding the WITH COMPRESSION clause
Using RESTORE instead of BACKUP
Nothing — SQL Server detects it automatically based on the file name
questions.explain: Without WITH DIFFERENTIAL, BACKUP DATABASE always produces a full backup. The clause is what makes it incremental relative to the last full.

questions.q: What does WITH NORECOVERY do during a RESTORE statement, and when should you use it?
options: It keeps the database in a restoring state so additional backups can be applied on top — use it on every restore step except the last one in the chain
It permanently deletes the database being restored
It skips restoring the transaction log entirely
It is only valid for full backups, never for differential or log restores
questions.explain: NORECOVERY leaves the database unavailable but ready to accept more restores. Recovering too early with WITH RECOVERY brings the database online but blocks applying any further backups.

questions.q: Why does this lesson's T-SQL syntax apply to on-prem and VM-hosted SQL Server but not Azure SQL Database?
options: Azure SQL Database does not expose BACKUP DATABASE or RESTORE DATABASE — Microsoft manages backups on its own schedule instead
Azure SQL Database uses entirely different SQL syntax for every operation, not just backups
BACKUP DATABASE only works over a VPN connection
On-prem SQL Server cannot run differential backups, only Azure SQL Database can
questions.explain: Azure SQL Database is a managed PaaS service — Microsoft owns the backup schedule and mechanism. This is the specific subject of the next lesson.

questions.q: What real advantage does the SSMS Restore Database GUI dialog offer over hand-writing every RESTORE statement?
options: It reads backup history from msdb and automatically proposes a valid restore chain, including a point-in-time slider for log backups
It restores databases faster than T-SQL because it uses a different engine
It is the only way to restore a differential backup at all
It automatically deletes old backup files after a successful restore
questions.explain: The dialog is genuinely useful for building a correct chain from backup history, and it includes a Script button to turn that plan into verified T-SQL.

questions.q: What is the practical consequence of using WITH RECOVERY (or omitting the clause) too early in a multi-step restore chain?
options: The database comes online, but you can no longer apply the remaining backups in the chain on top of it
SQL Server automatically continues applying the rest of the chain anyway
It has no effect — RECOVERY and NORECOVERY behave identically mid-chain
It converts the remaining log backups into full backups automatically
questions.explain: RECOVERY rolls back uncommitted transactions and brings the database online, which closes the door on applying further backups from the same chain.
